note: make board-post NOTE=... reaches /bin/sh and is re-split, so TWO CHARACTER CLASSES SILENTLY CORRUPT A NOTE. Backticks run as command substitution: a note naming a backtick-quoted identifier posted with that identifier replaced by nothing, stderr said command not found, and THE POST STILL SUCCEEDED and returned an id, so there is no failure signal. Double quotes inside the note break argument parsing outright, exiting 2 with expected key=value, got <word>. Both are natural to write -- code spans and quoted output are how you would describe anything technical. Use plain text only in NOTE, and read the post back with make board before trusting it. Cost three attempts and one redact to establish.
